newsitem.title: USA: Dole hits Clinton on domestic, foreign policy.
newsitem.headline: Dole hits Clinton on domestic, foreign policy.

text.p: Bob Dole on Tuesday accused President Bill Clinton of harming America's prestige overseas and doing too little to spur the U.S. economy as he wrapped up a four-day campaign swing through this key state.

"We are fighting for California, for every vote up and down this place," the Republican presidential nominee told the World Affairs Council of Orange County as he criticised Clinton as weak on foreign policy and repeated his contention that the president's plan for targeted tax cuts would do little.

"You may have heard my opponent say he is building a bridge to the future ... So far as entrepreneurs and developers of new technologies are concerned, the Clinton administration is more like a wrecking crew than a bridge-builder," Dole said.

"They talk about high technology ... as if it were created by magic -- and taxes and regulations had nothing to do with it," Dole said, making a pitch for his plan to cut income taxes by 15 percent and halve the capital gains tax rate.
He criticised Clinton for failing to stand up to Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein and hold together the international coaltion former President George Bush developed during the Gulf War.

"When President Clinton finally took military action in response to Iraq's invasion of the north, his cruise missile attack had more impact on CNN than it had on Saddam Hussein," Dole said, noting CNN had broadcast the volley live.

Making an all-out push to win California, which has 54 of the 270 Electoral College votes needed to win the White House, Dole concentrated on illegal immigration, endorsing a California ballot measure on Monday to end many affirmative action programmes.
From California Dole was to travel to Colorado and spend the night in Washington, D.C.
But after that it was anyone's guess. As the campaign entered its final week, Dole's aides were scrambling to figure out which states to focus on and constantly reassessing polls.
Until late on Monday the campaign had no idea where Dole would be spending Tuesday night and Wednesday's schedule was only agreed to at midday on Tuesday.

Dole was obviously quite eager to get home for the night, telling the crowd that he hoped to be home before Washington's National Airport closed at 10 p.m. EST (0300 GMT Wednesday). One sign of the problems Dole was having in California was the location of his Tuesday speech -- Orange County, usually a reliable Reupblican stronghold.
A Los Angeles poll showed Dole leading by only four points in the highly conservative county. Statewide the latest California poll showed Clinton leading by 20 points.
Even with a friendly audience, Dole sounded defensive at times as he tried to sell his plan for a $548 billion tax cut and balanced budget.
"Now you've heard Bill Clinton say that our programme would 'blow a hole in the deficit.' I think that's just a lot of hot air," Dole said.
